Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTA) with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 1994; entered into force 1995)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (negotiated and agreed in principle in 2020; ratification suspended — not currently in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (notably by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, imposing professional obligations on obliged entities including notaries; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 January 2019 concerning the identification of beneficial owners. UBO Register: Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), as amended by the Law of 6 July 2023 implementing the CJEU rulings of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20) which restricted public access. Company law: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (consolidated version of 2016), SARL provisions (Articles 180-1 to 180-27). Establishment licensing: Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions (autorisation d'établissement).

stage_2.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds for wastewater, VOCs, or waste handling

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Inland Revenue for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; central electronic portal: guichet.lu (business registration and tax identification).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For non-resident taxable persons: submit the VAT registration form to the AEDT to obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number. For establishing a SARL: execute incorporation deed before a Luxembourg notary, file with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the RCS e-Desk; the RCS process automatically issues the national business and tax identification number (n° d'identification), which is also used for VAT; no separate TIN application is required for direct taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists; statutory elections available include VAT groups (assujetti unique), fiscal unity for corporate income tax (intégration fiscale), and election to apply Luxembourg’s participation exemption regime for qualifying dividends and capital gains; ATAD hybrid mismatch rules apply without elective deployment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for established small businesses; non-established foreign suppliers must register from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg, subject to reverse-charge rules if applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time clearance or digital stamping regime. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to suppliers to Luxembourg public authorities (B2G) using Peppol BIS XML or Factur-X; B2B and B2C invoices can be issued electronically under EU invoicing rules without tax authority clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU are subject to 0% VAT where the goods are removed from the EU within statutory time limits and the exporter maintains full evidence of export. Services to non-EU business customers qualify for 0% VAT when the place of supply is outside Luxembourg under place-of-supply rules; hotpot dining services physically performed overseas fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsubstantiated zero-rating claims trigger retrospective VAT assessment, monthly default interest at 0.8%, fines of up to twice the tax evaded, and criminal penalties (imprisonment up to five years); statute of limitations extends from five to ten years in cases of tax fraud. Directors may be joint and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB); banking prudential supervision and AML/CFT enforcement are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full euro convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions under Article 63 TFEU. No exchange-control authorization is required for dividend remittance, franchise royalty payments, condiment-import settlements, intra-group loans, or equity injections. Dividend distributions by an SARL remain subject to the solvency and net-asset test under the Luxembourg Companies Act of 10 August 1915, as amended, shareholder approval at a general meeting, and a 15% domestic withholding tax, which is commonly reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) or to a lower treaty rate where the parent qualifies. Profit repatriation impediments are limited to standard corporate documentation, statutory audit thresholds, and statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the BCL for aggregated annual cross-border flows exceeding EUR 12.5 million.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion timeline, or compulsory repatriation threshold exists under Luxembourg law. Foreign-currency export receipts may be retained indefinitely in accounts held with CSSF-regulated credit institutions. The only binding requirements are: (i) statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL for aggregate annual flows exceeding EUR 12.5 million; (ii) physical cash-courier declaration under EU Regulation 2018/1672 for cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more; and (iii) standard customs, VAT, and trade-invoice documentation for hotpot-condiment exports and imports. Treasury policy recommends internal conversion of material foreign-currency balances into EUR within 30 business days to dampen CNH/USD exposure, but this is an internal governance rule, not a legal surrender mechanism.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Blocked Funds Account for statutory SARL share-capital subscription
Operational EUR Current Account with SEPA, SWIFT, and POS merchant-acquiring settlement
Capital Escrow Account (séquestre bancaire) supporting the notary's blocking attestation for the EUR 12,000 minimum share capital
Operational EUR/USD Current Account with trade-finance and import letter-of-credit capability
Operational Treasury Account with multi-currency sweep, short-term deposits, and FX-forward execution
Local SME Operational Account for payroll, rent, utility, and CIT settlement standing orders
Secondary Operational Account for merchant acquiring and intra-EU condiment-supply payables
Ancillary EUR Account for hedge collateral and cross-border settlement contingency

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rated Medium as a supplementary treasury rail and Low as a primary banking layer. Only CSSF-licensed electronic money institutions, or EU-EEA EMIs validly passporting under PSD2, may lawfully hold payment funds for a Luxembourg SARL. Offshore digital EMIs licensed in the United Kingdom, Hong Kong, or Singapore, without an EU passport, are legally incapable of issuing the bankers' blocking attestation required by the Luxembourg notary for the statutory capital-blocage, and expose treasury funds to safeguarding limitations and redemption mechanics under Directive 2009/110/EC. Fintech EMIs are therefore usable only for ancillary, low-value, and capped disbursements (e.g., condiment-sample purchases, small vendor outpayments), with mandatory daily sweeping to a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution and absolute exclusion from the equity-injection and capital-escrow workflow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory at initial onboarding for at least one authorized European director, or a Luxembourg/European based delegate holding a notarized power of attorney, attending an in-person client-acceptance interview at the Luxembourg bank's premises. Fully remote legal-entity onboarding is not offered by Tier-1 Luxembourg banks for non-resident-owned SARLs; e-IDAS-qualified electronic signatures and video-identification calls are accepted only as supplementary verification after the physical interview. The bank must also verify the identity of every UBO, director, and signatory against the RCSL excerpt, the RBE register, and certified passport copies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner resident in the People's Republic of China or Hong Kong SAR holding more than 25% of the SARL through a multi-tier holding chain, generating source-of-wealth and layered-structure scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing extract, notarized and apostilled corporate ownership chart from the ultimate shareholder down to the Luxembourg SARL, certified passports of all UBOs with a >25% interest, a written source-of-wealth letter covering the share-capital subscription funds, 12-month bank statements of the subscribing parent entity, group audited financial statements, and a documented commercial rationale for the Luxembourg holding and direct-operated hotpot chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative-news or sanctions screening flags attributed to Asia-Pacific condiment supply-chain counterparties, freight forwarders, procurement agents, or franchise partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated World-Check and consolidated EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening snapshots for each counterparty, a physical-trade evidence trail comprising import customs declarations, bills of lading, commercial invoices, logistics agreements, and tax-identification verification, plus a negative-news remediation memorandum prepared by the appointed Luxembourg AML compliance officer documenting absence of sanctioned individuals and the closure of red flags.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA and CRS classification ambiguity where the SARL is owned by non-EU shareholders through a Hong Kong or Chinese parent, raising a risk of misclassification, misreporting, or opaque-structure determinations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed CRS self-certifications on the Luxembourg standard form (Form 5900) for all account holders, Form W-8BEN-E or W-9 for FATCA indicia, tax-residence certificates issued by the relevant Chinese and Luxembourg tax authorities, and a documented CRS/FATCA data-flow matrix confirming the SARL's Luxembourg tax residence and entity-level taxable classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-incorporation or in-formation account opening: the SARL is not yet registered, and the bank is asked to open a blocked capital account without a final RCSL extract, creating signature-capacity and formation-structure risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized draft articles of association with the subscribed-capital schedule, the notary's written instruction letter to the bank, a draft RCSL incorporation excerpt, certified identification documents of all founding directors, and a signed undertaking freezing withdrawals from the bloqueur until the RCSL registration certificate is delivered.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive restaurant operations: daily POS cash takings, multi-store float movements, and condiment-supply receivables perceived as a money-laundering layering or commingling vector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-integrated POS acquiring contract with automated end-of-day settlement to the operational bank account, a treasury cash-management policy requiring cash-in-transit collections with tamper-evident seals, monthly reconciliation of cash deposits against POS terminal reports, an operational cash-handling procedure, appointment of an internal AML compliance officer, and a documented transaction-monitoring protocol covering the Low_Risk_Standard banking-AML risk tier of ISIC 5610 full-service dining.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The statutory SARL minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 (minimum paid-up portion EUR 3,000, being 25% of the subscribed capital) must be injected by the non-resident parent via SWIFT MT103 into the SARL's dedicated blocked capital-escrow account at the Luxembourg relationship bank. The SWIFT remittance information must state 'Subscription of SARL share capital - incorporation of LU_SARL' together with the relevant notary's file reference, and where the sending jurisdiction applies a purpose-code regime (e.g., SAFE code 621011 for outward direct investment from China), that code must be quoted in the payment header. The bank issues the statutory blocking attestation to the Luxembourg notary, the notary files incorporation with the RCSL, and the funds are released to the operational account only upon presentation of the final RCSL extract. For inbound transfers of EUR 10,000 or more, the bank applies origin-of-funds verification under Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended); no prior CSSF or BCL authorization is required for inbound equity in a dining-chain SARL, and the group's Low_Risk_Standard tier supports streamlined documentary processing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for hotpot-ingredient procurement, condiment supply-chain logistics, franchise-vendor payouts, and intra-EU food-service disbursements are cleared through (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV wires in EUR, USD, or CNH for direct supplier payments; (ii) UCP 600-compliant commercial letters of credit for bulk condiment and restaurant-equipment imports from Asian suppliers, with the Luxembourg bank issuing or confirming the LC; (iii) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for recurring mid-value consignments; (iv) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for intra-EU payroll, rent, utility, and vendor obligations; and (v) bank-integrated POS merchant acquiring with T+1 EUR settlement for dining revenues. A multi-currency settlement account may be held at the relationship bank, but must be swept same-day into the EUR master operating account to enforce centralized liquidity control and to mitigate mismatches between CNH/USD import payables and EUR-denominated merchant receipts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forwards and FX swaps executed with the Luxembourg relationship bank under an ISDA master agreement or FX Global Code-aligned framework
CNH/USD and CNH/EUR non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted through a CSSF-regulated credit institution, supported by documented underlying hotpot-condiment import and supply-chain exposures
Vanilla EUR/CNH and EUR/USD FX options (premium-paid) under the ISDA 1998 FX Definitions for revenue and gross-margin protection
EUR/USD and EUR/CNH cross-currency swaps for the management of medium-term intra-group loan exposures, subject to EMIR trade-reporting to an authorized trade repository and BCL statistical reporting

Collateralized OTC forward contracts compliant with EMIR regulatory technical standards, including counterparty due-diligence documentation and margin arrangements acceptable to the Luxembourg treasury

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (balance sheet, profit and loss account, and notes) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and publication in RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after each financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal notice and court-ordered astreinte (per-diem penalty); directors/managers are exposed to criminal fines up to EUR 10,000; failure to file for three consecutive financial years may result in administrative strike-off (radiation) by the RCS after prior RESA publication.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by the Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual general meeting approving the annual accounts; initial filing within one month of incorporation and within one month after any shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or false confirmation subjects the SARL to fines of EUR 5,000 to EUR 25,000 and each manager to fines of EUR 1,250 to EUR 12,500; non-compliance may also be published in RESA and access to the RBE restricted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé is required if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following at the financial year-end: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average headcount of 50 employees. Otherwise the SARL qualifies as a small undertaking and is exempt from statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (LUX GAAP) under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and annual accounts, transposing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted only for listed undertakings; accounts must be prepared in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, within one month after the general meeting approving the annual accounts, the SARL must log into the RBE portal and either reconfirm the existing beneficial ownership data or file an updated declaration. Any share transfer must be registered in the statutory share register and, when effective, the UBO register must be updated within one month of the transfer.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate combined Luxembourg City headline rate (17% corporate income tax / IRC + 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC + 6.75% municipal business tax); standalone IRC statutory rate is 17%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist. Reduced 15% IRC rate applies to the first €175,000 of taxable income; 80% IP-box exemption applies to qualifying self-developed IP income resulting in an effective rate of approximately 5.2%; investment tax credits are available for eligible digital, energy-transition and environmental equipment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and annex Form 34 (Cross-Border Controlled Transaction Statement), filed electronically through the MyLux e-filing portal of the Administration des contributions directes using LuxTrust/eID authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly advance CIT and municipal business tax prepayments are due on 10 February, 10 May, 10 August and 10 November of the current tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a Luxembourg SARL with a 31 December fiscal year-end, the statutory filing deadline is 31 December of the following calendar year. Administrative extension to 30 June of the second year is generally available for e-filed returns prepared by an approved Luxembourg tax adviser; the tax administration may request earlier filing via formal notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Luxembourg RCS registration number and national business register number of the SARL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not enter this field; the SARL, as resident taxpayer, must file under its Luxembourg RCS identity. Non-resident investors are identified in the shareholder schedule and Form 34.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1c / Legal Form and Corporate Seat
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form (Société à Responsabilité Limitée), registered office address and place of effective management of the Luxembourg entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For tax residence, register the SARL's central administration within Luxembourg. A non-resident shareholder cannot use this field to claim fiscal residency in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit computed under Luxembourg GAAP after commercial-law adjustments, including depreciation, provisions, disallowed expenses and non-deductible corporate taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SARL has an overseas permanent establishment in the hotpot-restaurant market, treaty-controlled foreign PE income is removed through elimination-of-double-taxation schedules, not by exclusion in the SARL's own declaration absent a Luxembourg-PE entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from prior years offset against current-year taxable income, subject to ownership-continuity and same-business-condition rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forwards claimed by a Luxembourg resident SARL must be traced to the Luxembourg taxpayer's own permanent establishments; losses of an overseas foreign restaurant branch cannot be offset in Luxembourg unless they belong to a Luxembourg PE under DTA PE rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of cross-border transactions between the Luxembourg SARL and non-resident related enterprises, including royalty, management fees, loans, condiment-supply and overseas restaurant management contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All controlled transactions exceeding the administrative Form 34 threshold must be declared; the related non-resident counter-parties must be identified by country, type and amount of transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Foreign Tax Credit and Treaty Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for DTA elimination of double taxation, including foreign underlying taxes, foreign PE taxes and withholding taxes on inbound dividends, interest or royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief is only available where the overseas PE profit is included in Luxembourg taxable income and the other Contracting State levies tax under an applicable DTA. Supporting tax-residence certificates of foreign taxpayers must be retained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after formal notice may trigger a surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax under Article 166 LIR, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%. Deliberate misdeclaration or fraudulent omission of revenue can lead to additional penal assessments, criminal fines of up to €250,000 and imprisonment of the responsible managers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions by a resident SARL, unless reduced or exempted. Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies at 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholder holding at least 10% for 12 continuous months; DTA rates may reduce the 15% statutory rate depending on the treaty and beneficial-ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief at source, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver an up-to-date foreign tax-residence certificate in OECD format to the Luxembourg paying agent before the dividend payment, confirm beneficial ownership and ownership duration, and submit the relevant treaty-relief statement/affidavit. Where the relief cannot be applied at source, the non-resident shareholder must claim a refund from the Administration des contributions directes within the applicable five-year limitation period. A Luxembourg tax residence certificate is likewise required when the shareholder is being treaty-relieved in the foreign source jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose domestic withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments by a Luxembourg company to non-resident beneficial owners. No Luxembourg withholding tax arises on IP royalties or debt interest absent a Luxembourg permanent establishment of the payee. Treaty rates therefore generally have no Luxembourg source-taxing role; however Luxembourg interest-limitation rules, CFC rules, transfer-pricing requirements and ATAD substance principles apply to intra-group royalty and interest arrangements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue threshold triggers mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting under EU DAC4; Luxembourg does not impose a separate fixed statutory EUR threshold for Local File/Master File, but OECD-compliant contemporaneous documentation must be available upon tax-audit request. Form 34 must be filed for cross-border controlled transactions exceeding the applicable Luxembourg administrative filing threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations to ordinary SARLs. Substance requirements are nonetheless embedded in OECD transfer-pricing rules, CJEU case-law principles (Cadbury Schweppes), Luxembourg CFC rules, DAC6 disclosure and beneficial-ownership/treaty-shopping jurisprudence. If adopted, the proposed EU Unshell Directive / ATAD 3 would require minimum indicators of substance for shell entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Offshore Profit Diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Luxembourg SARL operates overseas direct-operated hotpot restaurants but books revenue through a controlled foreign commissionaire or related Hong Kong/PRC service company, fails to declare taxable Luxembourg profits, omits cash restaurant revenue, or artificially strips hotpot restaurant profits through non-arm's-length management and supply contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional corporate income tax and municipal business tax assessment on the full concealed worldwide income, 10% late-filing/omission surcharge after formal notice, monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%, and penal tax-interest accumulation. Wilful tax fraud is a criminal offense carrying fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment for responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A gérant who signs false tax returns or directs concealment can be held jointly and severally liable for restitution of the tax deficiency, civil damages to creditors and minority shareholders, and in criminal proceedings may face disqualification from managing companies, travel restrictions and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation exists for the related-party hotpot brand royalty, condiment supply, loan or overseas restaurant management services; the Luxembourg SARL omits Form 34 or applies an undocumented royalty rate; profit allocation cannot be supported under the arm's-length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax authorities may recompute the taxable base at the arm's-length normal value, deny deductibility of excessive royalty/interest or management fees, impose a surcharge up to 10% of the additional tax after formal notice and charge 0.6% monthly late-interest. Serious false-record offenses trigger criminal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the gérant may be personally liable for civil restitution where gross negligence in TP documentation caused the company's tax loss; criminal liability and travel bans may arise where false documentation was knowingly used as instruments of tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Luxembourg SARL is a mailbox entity without office, employees, local board decisions or operational functions; it merely routes royalties, dividends or interest to a low-tax jurisdiction while claiming Luxembourg tax residence and treaty benefits; the overseas hotpot restaurants are managed entirely outside Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative recharacterization of the structure, denial of a Luxembourg tax-residence certificate, denial of treaty and Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits, CFC inclusion of shifted profits at the shareholder level, and in the event of the EU Unshell Directive, additional penalties for shell entities, including deemed income adjustments and exchange-of-information enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors facilitating sham-board structures can be prosecuted for forgery, abuse of corporate form and tax fraud; civil liability includes disgorgement and restitution; criminal proceedings may impose travel bans, confiscation and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Cash-Handling and Authorised Economic Operator Risks
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cash-basis overseas hotpot POS revenues are underreported or laundered through related suppliers; the SARL and its foreign subsidiaries fail to apply know-your-customer, source-of-funds checks or suspicious-transaction reporting; unlicensed remittance and condiment-import payment rails violate Luxembourg AML/VAT compliance standards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Luxembourg AML Law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) against legal persons can reach up to €5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; additional VAT assessments, customs penalties and disqualification of firms from European payment institutions may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and executive officers are civilly and criminally liable for AML violations, including direct orders for restitution and personal fines; in money-laundering cases, responsible gérants face deprivation of liberty, travel bans and professional disqualification from management functions.
